transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is… it’s gotten hard for people to understand me, especially at work. I’m a supervisor in retail, so I’m supposed to be explaining things clearly, like inventory numbers, the weekend schedule, who’s covering what shift, that kind of thing. But lately when I start talking, it’s like the words don’t stay in the right lane.

I’ll be trying to explain, say, the truck delivery numbers, and then I’m suddenly talking about Thursday, and then something about the church grill pops in, and then I’m thinking about my boss’s tone of voice from earlier, and I can see people’s faces change. They look at me like they’re waiting for the point, or like they lost the map of what I’m saying. And I know I started with one thing, but by the time I hear myself, it’s gone somewhere else.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I do know the work. I’m not new at it. But when I try to lay it out, especially out loud, it starts jumping around, and people can’t follow me. That’s the main reason I came in.
Lately, have you been feeling unusually energized or keyed up?

Unusually energized? I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I don’t really feel like I’ve got some big extra burst of energy or anything. If anything, I feel kind of… wound up in moments, maybe, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean by keyed up.

Like at work, I can be on edge because I’m trying to keep track of what I’m saying and how people are reacting, and then I notice myself getting tense. But I haven’t been walking around feeling unstoppable or extra charged up, if that’s what you’re asking. I’m not sure.
Have you been feeling unusually happy or euphoric lately?

Unusually happy? No, I don’t think so. Not like… euphoric, like on top of the world or anything. I don’t really have that.

I mean, there are moments where something is funny or I’m relieved if a work thing goes okay, but that’s just normal, I think. Mostly I wouldn’t describe my mood as especially happy. I haven’t noticed myself being overly cheerful or excited in that way. If anything, I’d have to ask what you mean by euphoric, because that sounds stronger than anything I’ve been feeling.
Have you started believing things that other people say aren’t true?

I’m not sure how to answer that exactly. I mean, I don’t think I’ve started believing anything that people are directly saying, “That’s not true,” if that’s what you mean. Nobody’s sat me down and said, “You’re wrong about reality,” or anything like that.

Sometimes people don’t follow what I’m saying, and then I start wondering whether I explained it badly or whether they misunderstood the order of things, but that feels different from believing something strange. I don’t think I have some fixed idea everyone is arguing with me about. At least, not that I can point to.

So… no, I don’t think so. Or I guess I’d need an example of what kind of belief you mean.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual?

Needing much less sleep? I don’t think so, no. I mean, my sleep isn’t something I’ve been tracking hour by hour, so I don’t want to sound too certain, but I haven’t noticed that I’m getting by on just a little sleep and still feeling fine or anything like that.

Some nights I might not sleep great, but that’s different from not needing it, I think. If I’m short on sleep, I usually feel it. I don’t wake up feeling like, “Oh, I only got a few hours and I’m ready to go.” So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve been needing much less sleep than usual.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

Hearing voices when no one else is around… I don’t know. I mean, I wouldn’t describe it that way exactly. I haven’t had a clear experience where I’m sitting alone and I hear, like, a person talking to me as if they’re in the room and then I check and no one’s there.

Sometimes I can get caught up in my own thoughts, or I’ll think I heard something and then realize it was probably from outside or the TV or a neighbor or something like that. But that feels different from “voices,” at least the way I understand what you’re asking.

So, no, I don’t think I’ve been hearing voices like that. If you mean something more subtle, I might need you to explain what you mean.
Did this problem with your speech start after any head injury, seizure, or other medical illness?

No, not that I know of. I mean, I don’t remember hitting my head or having a seizure or getting some illness and then suddenly talking like this after. That’s not really how I think it started.

It’s more that I came in because when I’m trying to explain something ordinary at work, like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, it starts coming out wrong. I’ll be trying to say which truck came in, and then I’m talking about Thursday, and then somehow the church grill gets mixed in, and then my boss’s tone of voice, and people are looking at me like they can’t follow the path I’m taking. In my head it feels connected, but when I say it out loud, I can see I’ve lost them.

So no, I don’t think it was after a head injury or a seizure or anything medical like that. It’s more this problem with getting the words to stay in order.
While this speech problem has been happening, have there been times when your mood felt abnormally high or irritable?

Abnormally high or irritable… I don’t think so, not in the way you probably mean. I mean, I get frustrated, sure, especially when I’m trying to say something and it’s not landing right, or people keep asking me to repeat myself and I can tell they’re getting impatient. That can make me irritated in the normal sense, like embarrassed and annoyed.

But I wouldn’t say my mood has been unusually high, like I’m on top of the world or wired or anything. And I don’t think I’ve been unusually irritable out of nowhere. It’s more tied to the situation, if that makes sense. If someone looks confused or cuts me off, I might feel myself getting tense, but I don’t think there have been stretches where my mood was just abnormally elevated or angry for no reason.

So… no, I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you found yourself caring much less than usual about things like work, hobbies, or spending time with other people?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way, exactly. I mean, I still care about work. I don’t want to mess things up there, and I’m aware when people are depending on me. It bothers me if I think I’ve made things harder for someone or if I haven’t explained something clearly enough.

Hobbies… I don’t know. I’ve never been the most hobby-oriented person, if that makes sense. I have things I do, or used to do more regularly, but it’s hard for me to tell if I’m caring less or if I’m just tired or preoccupied. Sometimes I don’t feel like doing much after work, but I don’t know that I’d call it not caring.

With people, I still care about them. I may not always feel like talking a lot, especially if I’m worried the conversation is going to get tangled up, but that’s different from not caring about spending time with them. So… I guess no, I haven’t really noticed a big drop in caring about those things. Or at least not one that stands out to me.
Have other people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to?

I don’t know that anyone has said it to me that way, no. Like, nobody has sat me down and said, “Your face looks flat,” or “Your voice sounds different,” not in those words.

Sometimes people ask if I’m tired, or they’ll say I seem quiet, but I don’t always know what they’re picking up on. It could just be that I’m concentrating on what I’m trying to say, or I’m trying not to get off track, so maybe my face is doing less than I think it is. I’m not really watching myself from the outside, you know?

My voice… I haven’t noticed it being less expressive, but I guess I wouldn’t necessarily be the best judge of that. At work I’m usually focused on getting the information across, and if people react strangely, I tend to think it’s because of the wording or the order I said things in, not because of my tone.

So, no, I haven’t really been told that directly. At least not that I can remember.
Have you had the feeling that other people can hear or know your thoughts, even when you haven’t said them out loud?

I’m not sure. I mean… not really, I don’t think. I’ve had moments where I wonder if someone is reacting to me before I’ve fully said what I meant, like they somehow already know where I’m going with it, but when I slow down and think about it, that could just be them reading my face or guessing from the situation.

I don’t have a clear feeling like, “They can hear my thoughts,” the way you’re asking. I’m pretty aware that if I haven’t said something out loud, then people shouldn’t know it. Sometimes I worry I’m being obvious somehow, like maybe my expression gives me away, or I’ve started to say something under my breath without realizing it, but that’s not exactly the same as them hearing my thoughts.

So… I guess my answer is no, not really. At least I haven’t noticed anything definite like that.
Have you felt that anyone was trying to harm you or deliberately send you special messages?

I don’t think so. Not in a clear way, anyway.

I mean, I can get uneasy about people sometimes, like if someone is looking at me too long or if there’s a strange tone in something they say, I might wonder for a minute what they meant by it. But I don’t really have a definite sense that someone is trying to harm me. I’m not walking around thinking there’s a plan against me or anything like that.

And special messages… I’m not sure what would count. Like, sometimes people say things and I’ll overthink whether there was a second meaning, especially if it connects to something I was already worried about. But that’s more me trying to interpret things, maybe too much, not like the TV or signs or strangers are sending me messages personally.

So I’d say no, not really. I haven’t noticed anything that I’d be confident calling that.
Have you ever felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside you?

No… I don’t think I’ve felt that, not in the way you’re saying. I know what you mean, like if a thought doesn’t feel like it belongs to me, or like somebody somehow placed it there, and I can’t really say that’s happened.

I do have thoughts that pop up suddenly, like anyone does, I guess. Sometimes I’ll be at work or at home and something will come into my head out of nowhere, and I’ll think, “Why am I thinking about that right now?” But it still feels like my mind doing it, even if it’s random or unwanted. It doesn’t feel like an outside person or machine or anything putting it there.

I might question myself about where a thought came from, especially if it’s distracting or odd timing, but I don’t have the feeling that it was inserted from outside me. So I’d say no, I haven’t noticed that.
Have you ever had a period when you felt so unusually confident or grand that you believed you had special powers, talents, or importance?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt good about something I did, or maybe more confident than usual if work was going well or I handled a situation better than I expected. Like if the staff listened to me or I fixed a problem, I might feel, you know, competent. But I don’t think I ever felt like I had special powers or that I was unusually important in some big way.

I’m trying to think if there was ever a stretch where other people would’ve said I was acting grand or full of myself, and… not really, at least not that I can point to. I can get ideas about how something should be done, and I might be stubborn if I think I’m right, but that feels different from believing I had some special talent beyond other people or some special role.

So I’d say no, I haven’t really had a period like that.
Have you had a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d describe it that strongly, no. I mean, I’ve had days where I feel low or kind of worn down, and sometimes it can sit with me for a while, but “depressed most of the day nearly every day” sounds like something more constant than what I can clearly point to.

I’d have to think about what counts as a “period,” too. Like, if you mean a couple of rough days here and there, then sure, I’ve had that. But if you mean weeks where almost every day I’m depressed for most of the day, I don’t know that I can honestly say yes. I haven’t really tracked it that way, so I might be missing the pattern, but nothing immediately comes to mind where I’d say, “Yes, that was happening nearly every day.”
For at least six months, have these problems with your speech and thinking been present most of the time?

Yeah… I think it’s been about that long. Around six months, maybe a little more or less, but six months is the number that sticks in my head.

At work, on the sales floor, people started noticing that I’d get kind of tangled up when I was explaining things. Like I’d start telling someone how we were handling stock or what needed to happen with a customer issue, and then I’d go around it in a strange way, or stop in the middle because I couldn’t quite get the next part lined up. It’s embarrassing, because I’m supposed to be the supervisor, so people look to me to be clear.

It hasn’t been every single minute, but it’s been there a lot of the time, enough that it’s noticeable. The jumbled explanations and those odd pauses or stops while I’m talking on the floor, that’s probably been going on for about six months now.
Compared with before this started, has your ability to do your job dropped noticeably?

Yes… yeah, it has. I don’t really like saying that, because I’ve been doing this kind of work a long time, and I used to be someone they could put in charge without thinking twice. But now I’m not trusted to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. Those used to be, you know, kind of my responsibility, or at least something I could handle. Now they’ll move someone else into that spot, or they’ll say it’s just “for coverage,” but it’s pretty clear they don’t want me handling the floor when it gets hectic.

And after my last performance review, my boss was pretty direct with me. He said if things don’t improve, I could be suspended. That was hard to hear. It wasn’t just, “Try to tighten this up,” it was more like a warning that my job is actually at risk.

It’s affected things at home too, not just work. My wife has had to pick up commitments I used to handle, because people started getting uncomfortable or confused around me. Like things I normally would’ve gone to or taken care of, she’s had to step in more. So compared with before, yes, my functioning has dropped noticeably.

I have things I do, or used to do more regularly, but it’s hard for me to tell if I’m caring less or if I’m just tired or preoccupied. Sometimes I don’t feel like doing much after work, but I don’t know that I’d call it not caring.

With people, I still care about them. I may not always feel like talking a lot, especially if I’m worried the conversation is going to get tangled up, but that’s different from not caring about spending time with them. So… I guess no, I haven’t really noticed a big drop in caring about those things. Or at least not one that stands out to me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are negative symptoms, especially reduced emotional expression, to help distinguish schizophrenia from schizoaffective disorder or unspecified psychosis.
doctor.question: Have other people told you that your face or voice seems less expressive than it used to?

target_item.reason: The question asks about reduced facial or vocal expressiveness, a negative symptom/affective flattening, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t know that anyone has said it to me that way, no. Like, nobody has sat me down and said, “Your face looks flat,” or “Your voice sounds different,” not in those words.

Sometimes people ask if I’m tired, or they’ll say I seem quiet, but I don’t always know what they’re picking up on. It could just be that I’m concentrating on what I’m trying to say, or I’m trying not to get off track, so maybe my face is doing less than I think it is. I’m not really watching myself from the outside, you know?

My voice… I haven’t noticed it being less expressive, but I guess I wouldn’t necessarily be the best judge of that. At work I’m usually focused on getting the information across, and if people react strangely, I tend to think it’s because of the wording or the order I said things in, not because of my tone.

So, no, I haven’t really been told that directly. At least not that I can remember.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are thought-broadcasting/passivity-type delusions, which would strongly support schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis over a transient psychotic disorder and help distinguish F20.0 from F29/F25.0.
doctor.question: Have you had the feeling that other people can hear or know your thoughts, even when you haven’t said them out loud?

target_item.reason: The question asks about thought broadcasting or others knowing/hearing thoughts, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure. I mean… not really, I don’t think. I’ve had moments where I wonder if someone is reacting to me before I’ve fully said what I meant, like they somehow already know where I’m going with it, but when I slow down and think about it, that could just be them reading my face or guessing from the situation.

I don’t have a clear feeling like, “They can hear my thoughts,” the way you’re asking. I’m pretty aware that if I haven’t said something out loud, then people shouldn’t know it. Sometimes I worry I’m being obvious somehow, like maybe my expression gives me away, or I’ve started to say something under my breath without realizing it, but that’s not exactly the same as them hearing my thoughts.

So… I guess my answer is no, not really. At least I haven’t noticed anything definite like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are any bizarre or persecutory delusions, which would help distinguish schizophrenia or acute psychosis from a mood-related psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: Have you felt that anyone was trying to harm you or deliberately send you special messages?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about persecutory or referential delusions, such as feeling harmed or receiving special messages, but the provided symptom profile does not include delusions or paranoia.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so. Not in a clear way, anyway.

I mean, I can get uneasy about people sometimes, like if someone is looking at me too long or if there’s a strange tone in something they say, I might wonder for a minute what they meant by it. But I don’t really have a definite sense that someone is trying to harm me. I’m not walking around thinking there’s a plan against me or anything like that.

And special messages… I’m not sure what would count. Like, sometimes people say things and I’ll overthink whether there was a second meaning, especially if it connects to something I was already worried about. But that’s more me trying to interpret things, maybe too much, not like the TV or signs or strangers are sending me messages personally.

So I’d say no, not really. I haven’t noticed anything that I’d be confident calling that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the disorganized speech occurs in the context of a psychotic symptom outside mood episodes by checking for thought insertion/control, which would support schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis over a transient/unspecified psychosis and help distinguish from schizoaffective disorder given absent clear mania so far.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that thoughts were being put into your mind by someone or something outside you?

target_item.reason: The question is about thought insertion, a psychotic experience where thoughts feel placed in the mind by an outside force. The provided symptom profile only covers disorganized thinking/speech, disorganized behavior, impairment, and duration, not thought insertion.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think I’ve felt that, not in the way you’re saying. I know what you mean, like if a thought doesn’t feel like it belongs to me, or like somebody somehow placed it there, and I can’t really say that’s happened.

I do have thoughts that pop up suddenly, like anyone does, I guess. Sometimes I’ll be at work or at home and something will come into my head out of nowhere, and I’ll think, “Why am I thinking about that right now?” But it still feels like my mind doing it, even if it’s random or unwanted. It doesn’t feel like an outside person or machine or anything putting it there.

I might question myself about where a thought came from, especially if it’s distracting or odd timing, but I don’t have the feeling that it was inserted from outside me. So I’d say no, I haven’t noticed that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a distinct manic episode, which would support schizoaffective disorder over schizophrenia-spectrum diagnoses.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period when you felt so unusually confident or grand that you believed you had special powers, talents, or importance?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about grandiose beliefs or manic/grandiose delusions involving special powers, talents, or importance, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt good about something I did, or maybe more confident than usual if work was going well or I handled a situation better than I expected. Like if the staff listened to me or I fixed a problem, I might feel, you know, competent. But I don’t think I ever felt like I had special powers or that I was unusually important in some big way.

I’m trying to think if there was ever a stretch where other people would’ve said I was acting grand or full of myself, and… not really, at least not that I can point to. I can get ideas about how something should be done, and I might be stubborn if I think I’m right, but that feels different from believing I had some special talent beyond other people or some special role.

So I’d say no, I haven’t really had a period like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been any major depressive episode, which would help distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia or acute/transient psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you had a period when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a depressive episode or persistent depressed mood, which is not covered by the provided symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I’m not sure I’d describe it that strongly, no. I mean, I’ve had days where I feel low or kind of worn down, and sometimes it can sit with me for a while, but “depressed most of the day nearly every day” sounds like something more constant than what I can clearly point to.

I’d have to think about what counts as a “period,” too. Like, if you mean a couple of rough days here and there, then sure, I’ve had that. But if you mean weeks where almost every day I’m depressed for most of the day, I don’t know that I can honestly say yes. I haven’t really tracked it that way, so I might be missing the pattern, but nothing immediately comes to mind where I’d say, “Yes, that was happening nearly every day.”

inference.note: F25.0 ruled out further: repeated denial of abnormally elevated/irritable mood, decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, and no clear depressive episode, making schizoaffective disorder less likely. Persistent disorganized speech without clear mood syndrome keeps schizophrenia vs unspecified nonorganic psychosis.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a continuous duration of psychotic/disorganized symptoms long enough to support schizophrenia rather than an unspecified psychotic disorder.
doctor.question: For at least six months, have these problems with your speech and thinking been present most of the time?

target_item.name: Psychotic Symptoms Duration
target_item.manifestation: The jumbled explanations and odd stops on the sales floor have been noticeable for about six months now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the speech and thinking problems have been present for at least six months, which directly concerns the duration of psychotic symptoms.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I think it’s been about that long. Around six months, maybe a little more or less, but six months is the number that sticks in my head.

At work, on the sales floor, people started noticing that I’d get kind of tangled up when I was explaining things. Like I’d start telling someone how we were handling stock or what needed to happen with a customer issue, and then I’d go around it in a strange way, or stop in the middle because I couldn’t quite get the next part lined up. It’s embarrassing, because I’m supposed to be the supervisor, so people look to me to be clear.

It hasn’t been every single minute, but it’s been there a lot of the time, enough that it’s noticeable. The jumbled explanations and those odd pauses or stops while I’m talking on the floor, that’s probably been going on for about six months now.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a clear decline in functioning, which would support schizophrenia over unspecified psychosis.
doctor.question: Compared with before this started, has your ability to do your job dropped noticeably?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’m not trusted to run busy weekend shifts anymore, and after the performance review my boss warned me I could be suspended if things don’t improve. At home, my wife has had to cover commitments I used to handle because people started getting uncomfortable or confused around me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the symptoms have caused a noticeable decline in work performance compared with before, which directly matches functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Yes… yeah, it has. I don’t really like saying that, because I’ve been doing this kind of work a long time, and I used to be someone they could put in charge without thinking twice. But now I’m not trusted to run the busy weekend shifts anymore. Those used to be, you know, kind of my responsibility, or at least something I could handle. Now they’ll move someone else into that spot, or they’ll say it’s just “for coverage,” but it’s pretty clear they don’t want me handling the floor when it gets hectic.

And after my last performance review, my boss was pretty direct with me. He said if things don’t improve, I could be suspended. That was hard to hear. It wasn’t just, “Try to tighten this up,” it was more like a warning that my job is actually at risk.

It’s affected things at home too, not just work. My wife has had to pick up commitments I used to handle, because people started getting uncomfortable or confused around me. Like things I normally would’ve gone to or taken care of, she’s had to step in more. So compared with before, yes, my functioning has dropped noticeably.

inference.note: Six months of prominent disorganized speech/thought with clear functional decline supports schizophrenia rather than unspecified nonorganic psychosis; mood episodes and medical causes were not supported, and no further questioning is needed.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a 6-month history of prominent formal thought disorder/disorganized speech with clear occupational and home functional decline, without evidence that the disturbance is due to mania, major depression, substance/medical causes, or a neurological event. Although classic positive symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions were denied, persistent disorganized speech is a core psychotic symptom and, in the context of sustained deterioration in functioning and duration consistent with schizophrenia-spectrum illness, supports paranoid schizophrenia (ICD-10 candidate provided).
